headline: Histology and spatial graphs now predict gene expression and spatial domains
label: Spatial Omics Computational Methods
summary: Paired H&E histology and spatial transcriptomics now let graph and generative models infer expression, cell communication, and spatial domains.
synthesis: The common thread is conditioning molecular inference on tissue context, either by predicting expression or cell states from H&E histology or by fusing histology with spatial transcriptomics. HistoPrism predicts gene expression from pan-cancer H&E and adds a pathway-level benchmark testing biologically coherent pathway readouts. miniMTI reconstructs a 40-marker multiplex panel from H&E plus three measured markers, and Hist2Cell predicts fine-grained cell-type abundance from histology images trained on lung and breast cancer data. COSMIC links nuclear morphology and gene expression through a bidirectional generative model pretrained on 21M nuclei. On the spatial transcriptomics side, HARMONIC infers spatially contextualized cell-cell communication from paired H&E, while stGCL, SpaConTDS, and AugGCL integrate expression, coordinates, or morphology in graph-based frameworks to identify spatial domains. What is new is the joint use of spatial graph priors and cross-modal fusion within a single model.
